text: dsh-block-hanging-commands 是一个面向 DSH Web 客户端的 shell 工具插件，在命令执行前检查可能等待人工输入或持续运行的前台命令。它解析命令并识别编辑器、交互式解释器、Git 交互操作、开发服务器、监听任务、日志跟踪和交互式容器等情况；匹配时可拒绝并给模型替代写法，或转为审批。可配置检查的 shell、规则、PTY 模式和正则放行条件，适合希望减少 agent 因 shell 命令挂起而卡住的用户。安装后不需要 API Key 或额外外部服务。

dsh-block-hanging-commands checks DSH Web shell commands for interactive or long-running cases such as editors, REPLs, servers, watchers, and Git prompts. It can deny with a suggested alternative or ask for approval. Configure checked shells and rules; no API key or external service is needed.
怎么避免 DSH 智能体运行交互命令后一直等着？
让 shell 工具拦住会等待键盘输入的命令，并给出非交互替代写法
我想阻止 agent 在前台启动开发服务器或 watch 任务
能不能在执行前识别不带提交说明的 git commit？
DSH 调用 python、node 这类空命令时总是卡住，怎么处理？
希望交互式 ssh、容器终端和持续跟踪日志不要挂住工具调用
How can I stop an AI agent from hanging on interactive shell commands?
Prevent foreground servers and file watchers from blocking a DSH turn.
dsh-block-hanging-commands 的功能「挂起命令拦截」：在 shell 工具执行前解析命令；发现命令会等待输入或持续运行时，返回拒绝原因和可尝试的替代写法，也可配置为询问审批。
dsh-block-hanging-commands 的功能「命令类别识别」：识别编辑器、REPL、Git 交互操作、开发服务器、监听和日志跟踪等命令，并为常见情形给出非交互替代方案。
dsh-block-hanging-commands 的功能「规则与放行配置」：可选择 deny 或 ask，禁用指定规则、配置始终放行的正则表达式，并选择需要检查的 shell 工具。
dsh-block-hanging-commands 的功能「终端与命令边界处理」：支持 POSIX shell 和 PowerShell 命令拆分，能考虑管道、重定向、输入来源、后台运行及超时等条件来判断是否应拦截。

dsh-block-hanging-commands README · dsh-block-hanging-commands：English | [中文](README_zh.md)

If you've used an agent for a while you've probably seen this. It runs `git commit` without `-m`, or `npm run dev`, or `python3` with nothing after it, and the turn just sits there. The command is waiting for a keyboard nobody is typing on. Usually the tool times out, the model learns nothing, and then it tries something just as bad.

dsh-block-hanging-commands README · dsh-block-hanging-commands：This plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) reads each shell command before it runs. If the command would wait for input or never exit, it doesn't run it. The model gets told why and what to run instead, so it can fix the call in the same step.

dsh-block-hanging-commands README · dsh-block-hanging-commands：```
dsh-block-hanging-commands stopped `git commit` before it ran, because `git commit`
without a message opens an editor, so the tool call would just sit there until it timed out.
Instead: pass the message: `git commit -m "<message>"` (or `--no-edit` when amending).
(rule: git-editor)

dsh-block-hanging-commands README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-block-hanging-commands
```

That's the `web` profile, the browser UI you start with `dsh web`. If you run DSH another way, use `headless` (scripts and CI) or `acp` (editor integrations) instead. Each profile keeps its own plugin list, so add it to every profile you use. That's all the setup there is. The plugin ships its own patch layer, so it's on as soon as it's installed.

To remove it: `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-block-hanging-commands`.

dsh-block-hanging-commands README · From a clone：To try local changes, build a tarball and install that:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/acus9345/dsh-block-hanging-commands
cd dsh-block-hanging-commands
npm install
npm pack

dsh-block-hanging-commands README · What it catches：| Rule | Examples | What the model is told to do instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editor` | `vim`, `nano`, `emacs`, `code --wait`, `subl -w` | use the edit tools or `sed -i` |
| `git-editor` | `git commit` or `git tag -a` without `-m` | pass `-m` / `--no-edit` |
| `git-interactive` | `git rebase -i`, `git add -p` | a plain rebase or `--autosquash` with `GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=:`; `git add <path>` |
| `repl` | `python`, `node`, `psql mydb`, `redis-cli`, `sqlite3 db` | `-c "..."`, a script file, or a heredoc |
| `server` | `npm run dev`, `vite`, `next dev`, `flask run`, `rails s` | `run_in_background: true`, or `timeout` |
| `watch` | `jest --watch`, `tsc -w`, `cargo watch`, `nodemon` | run once without the watch flag |
| `follow` | `tail -f`, `journalctl -f`, `kubectl logs -f`, `docker logs -f` | `tail -n 200`, `--since` |
| `remote-shell` | `ssh host` with no command | pass the command; `-o BatchMode=yes` |
| `container-tty` | `docker run -it`, `docker exec -it`, `kubectl exec -it` | drop `-it` |
| `tui` | `htop`, `top`, `lazygit`, `tig`, `ncdu` | the batch version (`top -bn1`, `git log`) |
| `prompt` / `login` | `npm init` without `

dsh-block-hanging-commands README · What it catches：It looks through the usual wrappers (`sudo`, `env`, `nohup`, `npx`, `pnpm exec`, `uv run`, `bash -c '...'`) and handles pipes, `&&` chains, heredocs and redirects. So `cd app && npm run dev` is caught, but `echo q | python3` and `python3 < script.py` are not, because their input is already there. `timeout 30 npm run dev` gets through, and so does any call made with `run_in_background: true`. In both cases the command is going to end or detach anyway. A dev server, watcher or `tail -f` called with the shell tool's own `timeoutMs` also gets through, since that bounds it the same way. An editor or prompt still doesn't, because a timeout just leaves it waiting in the background.

dsh-block-hanging-commands README · What it catches：It works on Windows too, where DSH runs commands through PowerShell (`pwsh`) instead of bash. There it also knows `npm.cmd`, full paths like `C:\Python312\python.exe`, the `&` call operator and `Get-Content -Wait`.

I tried hard to keep false positives down. `psql -c "select 1"`, `node script.js`, `vim -es`, `git commit -F msg.txt`, `top -bn1`, `ssh host uptime` and `--help` / `--version` on anything all pass.

dsh-block-hanging-commands README · Settings：The easy way: open **Plugins** in DSH's sidebar, click **dsh-block-hanging-commands**, change what you want and press **Save**. It applies to the next tool call, no restart needed.

Or put a row like this in `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, or in `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml` to cover every profile. Keys you leave out keep their defaults.

dsh-block-hanging-commands README · Settings：```yaml
- id: block-hanging-commands
  config:
    mode: deny             # or `ask` to get an approval prompt instead of a refusal
    tools: [bash, pwsh]    # shell tool names to inspect (pwsh is the Windows shell)

`pty` matters because without a terminal, `less` and `git log` don't page, and `sudo` fails instead of prompting. So those rules only switch on when the shell really is a PTY.

dsh-block-hanging-commands README · How it works：The plugin hooks `tools/pre-execute`. It tokenises the command itself (no shell is spawned), checks each simple command against the rules, and returns `deny` with the reason text if one matches. Nothing runs and nothing is rewritten. The model still decides what to do next. It's just deciding with better information.

dsh-block-hanging-commands README · Development：```sh
npm install
npm test           # unit tests for the command parser and rules
npm run test:e2e   # boots real dsh against a scripted local model, no API key needed
```

The install test runs `dsh plugin add`, which needs `pnpm` on your PATH.

The e2e suite also packs the plugin and installs it with `dsh plugin add`, the same way a user would, to make sure the published package actually loads.
